guidance: A geometric aid, not a navigation fix: the distances must refer to the same point, and the sphere ignores ellipsoidal flattening, terrain and measurement bias. Use more ranges and a proper error model for any real radio, GNSS or survey work.
method: Treat each station and the fix as unit vectors on a sphere of mean radius 6,371 km and measure distance as the central angle times the radius, using atan2 of the cross and dot products so the antimeridian needs no special case. Three distances are solved for the position by damped Gauss-Newton least squares in local east and north offsets: the residual at a station is the computed distance minus the measured distance, each Jacobian row is minus the sine and cosine of the bearing from the current estimate to that station, and the step solves the 2x2 normal equations with a Levenberg-Marquardt damping term that grows when a trial step does not reduce the root-mean-square residual. Iteration starts from the spherical centroid of the stations, from each station and from the antipode of the centroid, and the converged solution with the smallest residual is reported, which keeps the answer independent of the first guess. The fit is refused when the root-mean-square residual exceeds 1 km, when two stations coincide within 1 m, and when the stations are nearly collinear: the height of the station triangle above its longest side is compared with that side, and below 2 per cent the same distances also fit a position mirrored across the line, so no side is chosen. Distances are entered in kilometres, nautical miles (1.852 km) or statute miles (1.609344 km) and must lie below half the Earth's circumference. The geometry factor is the square root of the trace of the inverse of the normal matrix at the fix, in the same spirit as a horizontal dilution of precision; for three evenly spaced stations it is the square root of 4/3, about 1.1547, and values below 1.7 are labelled good, below 3 fair and above that poor. Coordinates accept a decimal point or comma, latitudes run from -90 to 90 and longitudes from -180 to 180, and blank, non-numeric, exponent-notation and out-of-range values are refused with the failing station and field named.
